turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes, Hale. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and did anyone speak to him before it went into the gradebook?
"Upset." I'm not here to be understood, Hale. I'm here for a name and a date, so who entered the zero, and what had Owen been asked before that?
But I'm not changing the grade.
"Not changing the grade." Then you'll tell me on what basis you gave it, because if there's nothing I can read, I'm going to the principal's office when we're done.
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.

I'm writing that down: "still not changing it," with no reason attached. Your own procedure, 4.2, says a parent is contacted before any mark consequence is entered, and nobody called me. So either you have something I can read, Hale, or I'm going upstairs.
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.

Then I'll have "no" in an email, Hale, with the date and time of this meeting on it. Procedure 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish a concern, so if the checker is all you have, say so now. If it isn't, show me what else there is.
